name: Fenwick Float
description:
Fenwick Float is a semi-permanent flotilla of linked barges, decommissioned ferry hulls, and modular platform sections anchored roughly two kilometers off the Chicago Lakeshore, accessible by water-taxi, private skiff, or the one functional mag-cable gondola that runs from a crumbling pier near the old Adler site. The Float began as an emergency housing overflow measure during the 2161 the Gray Zone flooding crisis and was never formally dissolved — it simply accumulated residents, commerce, and eventually its own internal logic, drifting slightly with seasonal anchor adjustments but always remaining within the same rough coordinates.

Because the Float sits in jurisdictionally ambiguous water — technically under GLMZ municipal charter but practically unreachable by standard Ferrogate ground patrols — it has become a preferred location for operations that require distance from civic scrutiny. Legitimate floating restaurants and water-purification co-ops share deck space with unlicensed medical clinics, data brokerage nodes, and at least two competing smuggling operations that have achieved a workable truce. The lake wind is constant and the horizon is always visible, which residents cite with surprising frequency as reasons they stay.

sights: The Float's connected platforms undulate gently in a slow, breathing rhythm, making every structure on it appear subtly, perpetually in motion.
String lights and bioluminescent algae panels illuminate the inter-platform walkways at night, reflecting in broken columns across the black lake surface.
Laundry, solar collection film, and signal-mesh antennae all compete for vertical space on every mast and railing, giving the Float a festive, cluttered skyline.
The mag-cable gondola arrives every forty minutes, its single cabin lit warm amber against the dark water, trailing a thin wake of spray.
sounds: The constant low percussion of lake swells against hull metal creates a rhythm that residents stop consciously hearing within days of arrival.
Competing music from the floating restaurant barges bleeds together across the walkways into a layered, accidental ambience.
The gondola cable hums a descending note as it approaches the Float's main dock, serving as the closest thing to a public clock the community has.
smells: Lake air dominates — clean and cold with an algal mineral edge that sharpens in the morning and softens at dusk.
Cooking smells from a dozen different culinary traditions drift and combine across the platform walkways, strongest near the central barge cluster.
Below the waterline access hatches, a persistent smell of treated bilge water and hull sealant rises whenever they are opened.
atmosphere.feel: There is a looseness to Fenwick Float that the city proper cannot replicate — the sense that the rules apply differently here, or not at all, or only the ones that residents have agreed to among themselves. The constant motion underfoot is disorienting for newcomers and becomes, for long-timers, a physical reassurance. The lake horizon provides a psychological expanse that the corridor's vertical density forecloses entirely.

demographics: A genuinely mixed population ranging from Tier 1 laborers who could not secure the Gray Zone housing to deliberate off-grid professionals (data brokers, unlicensed medics, gray-market logistics coordinators) to a small number of Tier 3 residents who maintain secondary residences here for privacy reasons.
economy: Tourism and food service from the restaurant barges, water purification co-op revenues, and a substantial gray-market economy centered on data brokerage, unlicensed medical services, and logistics coordination for contraband moving in and out of the Lakeshore Corridor.
power_structure: The Float has no formal governance; a rotating Harbor Committee handles platform maintenance and inter-operator disputes, but real authority is exercised by the two dominant smuggling operations — Carrion Logistics' unofficial lake division and an independent crew known as the Meridian Drift — who maintain their truce through mutual dependency.
dangers: Platform connection joints fail periodically, separating sections of the Float during storm conditions and stranding residents until emergency lashing can be rigged.
The jurisdictional ambiguity that protects the Float also means emergency services response times from the shore average forty-seven minutes — effectively nonexistent.
The Meridian Drift crew is volatile; their truce with Carrion Logistics has collapsed twice in six years, and both incidents produced casualties among uninvolved Float residents.
Arcturus Defense Solutions operates an intermittent aerial surveillance drone pattern over the lake, and the Float is logged in their tracking database as a 'person of interest aggregation site.'
opportunities: The Float's unlicensed medical clinic operates with equipment and pharmaceutical access that rivals some legitimate Tier 3 facilities, at a fraction of the cost and with no identity verification.
The data brokerage nodes on the Float maintain Diaspora connections routed through lake-bed relay buoys that are effectively invisible to standard municipal traffic monitoring.
Carrion Logistics' lake division offers reliable, quiet transport of persons and cargo to points along the entire Great Lakes coastline, no manifest required.
story_hooks: A Palladian Group corporate attorney arrived on the Float three weeks ago and has not left — she is not using her credentials, not contacting her firm, and the one Float resident who tried to speak with her says she seemed genuinely terrified. Someone from the Spire is now offering Φ15,000 for her safe return, and someone else is offering Φ20,000 for confirmation that she never makes it back.

The mag-cable gondola broke down mid-crossing yesterday with six passengers aboard, and when the maintenance crew finally reached it, four of the six were dead from apparent BCI-induced cardiac arrest — the other two have no memory of the crossing at all.

The water purification co-op has quietly discovered that the lake-bed relay buoys routing the Float's Diaspora connections are also carrying an encrypted secondary signal of unknown origin — one of the co-op's engineers believes it is an E.L.F. using the Float's infrastructure as a refuge node.
frequented_by: Gray-market data brokers and information traders
Off-grid Tier 3 professionals maintaining privacy residences
Carrion Logistics and Meridian Drift affiliated logistics personnel
Lakeshore Corridor residents seeking unlicensed medical or legal services

notable_locations.name: The Meridian Table
notable_locations.description: The Float's largest restaurant barge, serving a rotating menu sourced entirely from lake-harvested and vertical-farm stock — the best meal available outside the Spire, if you can get a reservation and find a way out here.

notable_locations.name: The Bilge
notable_locations.description: The below-waterline access corridor connecting the Float's oldest hull sections, used officially for maintenance and unofficially as the primary meeting space for dealings neither party wants conducted in open air.
